'''''Schoenoplectus pungens''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[Cyperaceae|sedge family]] known as '''common threesquare''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=SCPU10|taxon=Schoenoplectus pungens|accessdate=1 February 2016}}</ref> '''common three-square bulrush'''<ref name=fna>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242357940 Flora of North America]</ref> and '''sharp club-rush'''.<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> It is a [[herbaceous]] [[Emergent plant|emergent]] plant that is widespread across much of [[North America|North]] and [[South America]] as well as [[Europe]], [[New Zealand]] and [[Australia]].<ref name=tabby>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=263065 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref name=Wisplants>{{cite web|title=Family Cyperaceae Schoenoplectus pungens (Vahl) Palla|url=http://wisplants.uwsp.edu/scripts/detail.asp?SpCode=SCHPUN|publisher=Wisplants|access-date=4 February 2013}}</ref><ref>Jermy, C., Simpson, D., Foley, M. & Porter, M. (2007). Sedges of the British Isles. B.S.B.I. Handbook No. 1, ed. 3: 1-554. Botanical Society of the British Isles, London.</ref><ref>Govaerts, R. & Simpson, D.A. (2007). World Checklist of Cyperaceae. Sedges: 1-765. The Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew.</ref><ref>Castroviejo, S. & al. (eds.) (2008). Flora Iberica 18: 1-420. Real Jardín Botánico, CSIC, Madrid.</ref><ref>Rothrock, P.E. (2009). Sedges of Indiana and adjacent states: the non-Carex species: 1-271. Ukrayins'k Botanichnyi Zhurnal 66: 650-655.</ref><ref>Acevedo-Rodríguez, P. & Strong, M.T. (2012). Catalogue of seed plants of the West Indies. Smithsonian Contributions to Botany 98: 1-1192.</ref>

==Habitat==
Threesquare is found in open, sun-lit marshes and along the shores of lakes and ponds, in water up to {{cvt|1|m}} deep. It is resistant to fire.<ref name=CalFlora>{{cite web|title=Schoenoplectus pungens (Vahl) Palla|url=http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-calrecnum=10359|publisher=CalFlora|access-date=4 February 2013}}</ref><ref name=usda>{{cite web|title=Conservation Plant Characteristics|url=https://plants.usda.gov/java/charProfile?symbol=SCPUP5|publisher=USDA.gov|access-date=4 February 2013}}</ref><ref name=NativePC>{{cite web|title=Schoenoplectus pungens v. pungens (Scirpus pungens, Scirpus americanus)|url=http://www.nativeplantcenter.net/?q=plants/791|publisher=Native Plant Center|access-date=4 January 2013}}</ref><ref name=CalFloraPungens>{{cite web|title=Scirpus pungens Vahl three square|url=http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-taxon=Scirpus+pungens|publisher=CalFlora|access-date=4 February 2013}}</ref>

==Description==
''Schoenoplectus pungens'' is a long-lived perennial herb up to {{cvt|1.5|m}} tall.<ref name=usda/> The foliage is dark green, rough and dense. The small flowers are grouped in dense spikelets, with of 1–7 spikelets on each stem.<ref name=usda/> The seeds are brown.<ref name=usda/>

It is closely related to ''[[Schoenoplectus americanus]],'' and many ''Schoenoplectus pungens'' specimens have long been misidentified as ''Schoenoplectus americanus.''<ref name=fna/>
